edges.parent_basis:
The decree printed at the head of the edition states what it was made from and
to: the Pontifical Commission instituted by Pius X on 2 July 1911, having
prepared the typical edition of the Breviary approved 25 March 1914 to the norm
of Divino afflatu and Abhinc duos annos, turned the same norms on the Missal.
The edge therefore runs through the two acts it names, and not through any
printing that happens to fall between 1634 and 1920.
edges.via_unrepresented_basis:
The same decree says the text was drawn from the other typical edition, that of
1900: `In qua editione, ex altera typica anni 1900 deprompta, illud tantum
innovatum est, quod ex recentibus praescriptionibus liturgicis et ex additionibus
et variationibus, in Breviario typico inductis, consequeretur.` That edition is
not in this corpus and no act promulgating it is cited here, so the edge from the
1634 revision down to 1920 crosses at least one station this record does not
hold. It is drawn as descent, not as succession.

The quotation also bounds the 1920 edition's own reach, and is why this act
carries so few departures: it says that the only thing made new was what followed
from the recent liturgical prescriptions and from the additions and variations
introduced in the typical Breviary.
